QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_68

question.text: Under SAS-1300 the SIA should be CAUTIOUS about using 'Total savings by participants' as an impact indicator because:

answer.text: Savings can be driven by other factors (income shocks, demonetisation-style events, government DBT inflows) — the SIA must net out exogenous factors before claiming programme impact

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Savings-volume is confounded with exogenous shocks (DBT inflows, demonetisation cash movements, festival cycles). SAS-1300 attribution requires netting out these exogenous factors — typically via control-group or time-trend analysis. **The Trap:** Options B, C, D are not the primary concern. **Cross-Exam Context:** Confound-control logic in XV Research Analyst and XIX (AIF — performance attribution). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Split savings-growth into (i) account-opening effect, (ii) DBT pass-through, (iii) behavioural (true programme effect). Only (iii) is attributable to the SE — the other two are mechanical pass-throughs.
